title: Patient Financial Account — Good-Faith Percentage by Account Tenure
content:
The good-faith percentage of a final-notice paydown on the Patient Financial Account starts from the account's tenure, measured from the opening date recorded on the account to the handling date:

| Account opened | Tenure percentage |
|---|---|
| at least 120 calendar months before the handling date | 40 percent |
| at least 60 but fewer than 120 calendar months before | 50 percent |
| fewer than 60 calendar months before | 60 percent |

Every lowering or raising of the good-faith percentage is counted in percentage points from this starting figure.

**Counting months.** A window of calendar months for the final-notice paydown ends on the handling date and reaches back that many months, a date on the same calendar day that many months earlier falling outside it. An account opened on 10 March 2016 has, on a handling date of 10 March 2026, been open 120 calendar months and takes 40 percent; on 9 March 2026 it has been open fewer than 120 and takes 50 percent.

**Boundary pairs (hypothetical).**

- Opened exactly 60 months before the handling date: 50 percent. Opened 59 months and some days before: 60 percent.
- Opened 121 months before: 40 percent.

**Illustration of the point counting (hypothetical).** A tenure percentage of 50 lowered by 5 points is 45 percent; the same 50 raised by 10 points is 60 percent.
